jobs.description:
Director of Product Marketing

Remote, US

About Nametag
Nametag is building the future of secure digital identity. Our mission is to protect every human identity to restore trust in the AI era. We bring workforce-grade identity verification into the enterprise to verify the human behind accounts and critical actions. Today, global enterprises use Nametag across their workforce to prevent social engineering and deepfake impersonation attacks.

The Role

Nametag is hiring a Director of Product Marketing to own positioning, launch, and sales enablement for Nametag's core identity verification platform and its solutions; the account-recovery and helpdesk workflows most of today's revenue and pipeline run through. This is a senior, individual-contributor role for someone who has carried product marketing end to end at a B2B security company before: positioning that holds up under a CISO's scrutiny, launches that ship with sales enablement attached instead of following weeks later, and competitive claims a competitor's own product marketer would call fair. You'll be the person other teams turn to for the accurate, current answer on how Nametag describes itself across sales conversations, the website, analyst briefings, and every deck in between.

Role Overview

As Director of Product Marketing, you will own positioning and messaging for Nametag's core identity verification platform, and be the point of accountability for keeping that message consistent as the company grows quickly. You will lead messaging and materials creation for new product launches, build and maintain the sales enablement and competitive materials our go-to-market teams rely on daily, keep strict documentation of all product features and new releases, and partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Growth Marketing, Channel Partnerships, and Product Management. You’ll also have particularly close ties to the ITSM and IAM integration ecosystem (Okta, ServiceNow, Microsoft Entra ID, Zendesk).

What you’ll do

Positioning & Messaging

  • Own Nametag's core-IDV narratives, and serve as the arbiter of how they're positioned across every customer-facing surface.
  • Maintain and enforce the company's messaging and style guide: sourcing rules, canonical terminology, approved claims, so the same product doesn't end up with different language in the market at once.
  • Translate product capabilities into messaging that holds up for a CISO, a security/IAM leader, an IT leader, and a helpdesk leader; the buyers and influencers Nametag sells into.

Product Launches & Go-to-Market

  • Own the go-to-market plan for new core-platform and solution modules and features from kickoff to launch: messaging, positioning, sales enablement, and cross-functional coordination with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Sales.
  • Build repeatable launch frameworks: messaging pillars, soundbites, ICP and stakeholder mapping, objection handling, so each launch doesn't start from a blank page.
  • Define and track launch success metrics in partnership with Product Management and Marketing Ops.

Competitive Intelligence & Differentiation

  • Own competitive battlecards and differentiation materials against MFA/authentication vendors and consumer-grade KYC vendors expanding into workforce use cases, and keep them current as the market moves.
  • Research and articulate how Nametag's core verification differs from adjacent categories in terms a technical buyer will find credible, not dismissive.
  • Keep every competitive claim sourced and fair: testable against how the competitor would describe themselves.

Sales Enablement

  • Build and maintain the materials Sales, Customer Success, and Channel Partnerships use daily for deals: one-pagers, talk tracks, discovery questions, objection handling, and the master decks used with prospects.
  • Train Sales and Solutions Engineering on new positioning, features, and competitive intelligence.
  • Partner with Channel Partnerships on enablement for technology and reseller partners (e.g., ServiceNow, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID), so partner-sourced deals have the same quality of material as direct ones.

Analyst & Industry Relations

  • Brief industry analysts (e.g., Gartner, KuppingerCole) and manage Nametag's participation in relevant IAM/identity-verification research and reports, including our current Gartner Magic Quadrant Visionary recognition.
  • Represent Nametag's product story at industry events, webinars, and customer-facing presentations.

Pricing, Packaging & Proof

  • Own how Nametag communicates pricing and packaging for the core platform and solutions.
  • Maintain the ROI/TCO methodology used in sales conversations (e.g., helpdesk ticket reduction, cost-per-reset), with sourcing rigorous enough to survive a technical buyer's second look.
  • Develop customer stories and case studies with named accounts, in partnership with Customer Success, that hold up as proof rather than testimonials.

Customer & Market Research

  • Maintain and refine Nametag's IT/security ICP and buyer-persona models as the customer base grows into new verticals.
  • Stay current on the threat landscape and regulatory environment Nametag's customers operate in, and translate that into content and talking points Sales and Marketing can use.

What You Bring

We encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply, even if you don't meet every listed qualification. You'll thrive in this role if you bring most of the following:

  • 8+ years in product marketing, including several years at a B2B cybersecurity, identity, or enterprise security software company.
  • A track record of owning positioning and messaging for a technical security product, and making it hold up under scrutiny from CISOs and security/IAM leaders.
  • Experience leading product launches end to end: messaging, sales enablement, and cross-functional coordination, not just the content around the edges of one.
  • Deep fluency with enterprise security buyers and B2B security sales cycles; comfortable being precise about technical distinctions (e.g., authentication vs. verification) that matter to a technical audience.
  • Familiarity with the ITSM/IAM integration ecosystem (Okta, ServiceNow, Microsoft Entra ID, Zendesk) is a strong plus.
  • Strong competitive intelligence instincts: comfortable building battlecards and differentiation frameworks that are accurate and fair, not just favorable.
  • Experience partnering with industry analysts (Gartner, Forrester, KuppingerCole, or similar) is a strong plus.
  • Excellent, disciplined writing. Comfortable being the person who enforces consistent terminology and voice across a fast-moving team, not just the person who writes copy.
  • Experience with sales enablement tooling (e.g., HubSpot) and building or maintaining ROI/TCO models is a plus.
  • A strong sense of ownership: comfortable being the final word on message consistency at a small, fast-growing company where that job doesn't yet have a lot of scaffolding around it.
  • Enthusiasm for integrating AI tools like Claude into your everyday workflow; a keen sense of the difference between “AI slop” and AI-generated assets.

What We Value

  • Intellectual horsepower. Quickly grasping complex technical and business concepts.
  • Kindness and integrity. Earning trust is central to how we build relationships with customers and colleagues.
  • Bias for action. We move quickly to deliver impact and protect our customers against fast-moving threats.
  • Ownership mindset. You care about uptime and stability the way a founder cares about the product.

Culture & Perks

At Nametag, we believe trust starts with how we treat each other. We're a remote-first team that values autonomy, inclusivity, and collaboration, with regular in-person time to stay connected and innovate together.

  • Remote-first: Work from anywhere in the US. Our team spans Seattle, San Francisco, Ann Arbor, Denver, New York City, and beyond.
  • Off-sites: We bring the team together once per quarter for in-person collaboration, often off-site in new places.
  • Flexible schedules: Work in your own time zone; we align key meetings across a shared window.

We Offer

  • Competitive salary
  • Meaningful equity ownership
  • Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)
  • Flexible paid time off
  • Quarterly team off-sites and travel support
  • New computer hardware and equipment
  • An inclusive environment where your voice has impact and your work drives change

Cloud Accounting: AMLB takes the stress out of managing clients' day-to-day finances by providing a comprehensive cloud bookkeeping solution. From a digitized receipt capture solution to maintaining up-to-date financial records, we handle the clients' bookkeeping tasks efficiently and accurately. With WagePoint at the core, we manage direct deposits, T4 slips, tax remittances, and real-time updates, while leveraging collaborative tools to ensure accuracy, timeliness, and insight-driven payroll management.

CFO Advisory: Through virtual CFO services, AMLB delivers strategic financial guidance tailored to the needs of growing businesses. Our advisory offering includes financial modeling, deep dives into profit and margin leakage, audit committee and board reporting, cash flow and forecast analysis, and key performance indicator (KPI) development—all at a fraction of the cost of an in-house CFO.

Not-for-Profit Services: AMLB provides end-to-end financial compliance and advisory for not-for-profit organizations, including preparation and electronic filing of T3010 Registered Charity Returns, funder reporting, and support with government rebate programs such as HST, property tax, and public service body rebates.

Technology Enablement: AMLB stands out through its industry-leading use of cloud-first tools to automate, document, and streamline client services—leveraging platforms like Karbon for workflow management, SweetProcess and Loom for process documentation, Dext Prepare for receipt capture, QBO/Xero for accounting, WagePoint for payroll, Plooto for payments, and Microsoft SharePoint and Teams for seamless collaboration.

AMLB in the Community:

AMLB is a purpose-driven organization committed to improving outcomes for clients, team members, and its communities. We regularly support various causes, such as ending youth homelessness, reducing poverty, and eliminating its carbon footprint.

Become a part of our caring community

The Lead Actuary, Risk and Compliance is responsible for the overall management and oversight of actuaries and/or support staff where activities are concerned with identifying and managing risks. You will identify and analyze potential risks and estimates the potential financial consequences, develop and recommend controls and cost-effective approaches to minimize risks. You will work on problems of diverse scope and complexity ranging from moderate to substantial.

The Lead Actuary, Risk and Compliance will report to the Director, Actuarial Risk & Compliance. In this specific role, you will be part of a team tasked with assessment of risk, opportunities, and mitigation strategies to assure the compliant submission of bids to support Humana's pricing and product development of Medicare Advantage and Prescription Drug Plans that positively impact the financial performance of Humana. In particular, this position is responsible for ensuring compliance with CMS requirements related to Total Beneficiary Cost. This includes maintaining the internal version of the Out-of-Pocket Cost (OOPC) Model published by CMS, obtaining needed inputs from business partners, running and interpreting the model’s results, and partnering with the pricing actuaries to find solutions to resolving test failures.

In addition, as a member of the Compliance team this role is responsible for:

  • Supporting Humana’s MA-PD and PDP bid filings by ensuring appropriate interpretation and implementation of CMS guidance, and implementation and execution of review standards and controls to minimize compliance risk associated with the bid filing

  • Participate in CMS audits and reviews related to Humana’s Medicare bids.

  • Create and maintain process improvements to bid filings to continually improve Humana's ability to file compliant bids.

This position comes with the opportunity of leading a direct report.

The Lead Actuary, Risk and Compliance assesses and communicates information regarding actuarial/business risks across the organization. You will provide peer review and counsel on a wide variety of company, industry, and regulatory practices. Activities may include monitoring developments in actuarial techniques, and researching laws and regulations applicable to actuarial science and insurance operations. jobs.description:
Senior Telephony Engineer, Avaya Aura

Company Overview

Waterfield Tech enables companies to select, design, and deploy tailored customer engagement solutions from the world’s leading providers enhanced by cutting edge Applied AI. The results are happier customers, enhanced insights, and lower costs.

Once live, we empower companies to support, optimize, and modernize those solutions and AI applications, leading to lower risk and increased efficiency. Our client-centric process and track record of success have earned the trust of clients around the world when it comes to customer interaction.

We value our people—their diversity, their dedication, and their commitment to customer satisfaction. We encourage each other. We understand the value of hard work and the importance of a healthy balance. We’re all on the same page… even though we may get there from different perspectives. All in all, it’s a pretty cool place to be and we’re growing our global team of engineers, sales professionals, and creative souls.

Position Summary

Waterfield Tech is seeking a Senior Telephony Engineer, Avaya Aura to lead the hands-on deployment of complex Avaya Aura and unified communications solutions (on-premises, hybrid, and cloud) across commercial, enterprise, and government customers, increasingly including migration from legacy Avaya estates to cloud and CCaaS platforms.

The Senior Telephony Engineer owns the technical delivery of each engagement day to day, including configuration, integration, testing, and cutover, working closely with Waterfield Tech Project Managers to deliver on time, on quality, and to standard. As a senior technical resource, the engineer mentors less experienced voice engineers and contributes to delivery standards and reusable IP. Deep, hands-on Avaya Aura expertise is required; breadth across UC/CCaaS and cloud is valued.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the hands-on deployment of Avaya Aura solutions end to end (System Manager, Session Manager, Communication Manager, messaging, media servers and gateways, and IM & Presence (Breeze)) across on-premises, hybrid, and cloud, including virtualized and physical server builds (OVA deployment, VM sizing) in new and upgrade environments and applying service packs and patches per Avaya documentation.
  • Own day to day technical delivery (configuration, integration, testing, and cutover), managing schedules and adhering to stage gate quality and control standards across the full lifecycle, including issues, risks, and change requests, to ensure successful, on time delivery.
  • Perform discovery of customer telephony environments; gather requirements and complete data gathering for the Avaya Aura application servers; communicate network and system requirements (DHCP scope options, QoS, and split-horizon DNS).
  • Configure and deploy Aura call routing and edge, including dial plans (E.164 and shortcut dialing), Communication Manager vectoring/VDN where contact center functionality is required, SIP-based Remote Worker, Session Border Controller (SBCE), SIP trunking, and Avaya Workplace (formerly Equinox) soft clients across iOS, Android, Windows, and WebRTC, and troubleshoot as needed.
  • Lead certificate implementation end to end (CSR generation and installation of customer/Avaya certificates across the Aura stack); complete licensing via Avaya PLDS and technical onboarding via Avaya GRT.
  • Complete integration programming between Avaya Aura servers and to non-Avaya systems, and support adjuncts such as IVR, CMS reporting, call recording, and SIP PSTN services.
  • Validate and troubleshoot end to end connectivity using system tools and the Avaya knowledge base, and develop and execute acceptance test plans that evaluate the customer's Avaya Aura environment.
  • Support migration and modernization: legacy to cloud and hybrid Avaya migrations, and integration with CCaaS and AI-enabled capabilities such as virtual agents and agent assist.
  • Apply AI to delivery by using AI-powered tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, Claude) for documentation, testing, and delivery efficiency, and maintain accurate booking and time entry in Microsoft Dynamics 365/Project Operations.
  • Contribute to delivery standards, practices, templates, tools, and reusable IP that mature the Avaya practice, and provide coaching and mentoring for less experienced voice engineers.
  • Ensure delivery meets Waterfield Tech standards and remains compliant with RFP/proposal SOW and executed contract terms, and support pre-sales scoping, feasibility, and level of effort.
  • Continue professional development and Avaya certification, and perform other duties as assigned.

How This Role Is Measured

This role is measured on the delivery of assigned work and the quality of what is handed off. Primary measures are task estimate adherence (actual versus estimated hours on assigned WBS tasks) and on time task completion against the project plan, together with delivery quality: the rework rate on deliverables after handoff (lower is better) and first pass acceptance by the client or QA without revision.

Closeout and operational accuracy also matter: as-built documentation completed to standard and finished on or before the Day 2 handoff, and customer environment and credential records kept current in Keeper, updated within SLA of any go-live or change and passing spot check audit without correction. Finally, the engineer is expected to keep required Avaya certifications current, including Infinity Class 1+.

Primary Delivery & Technical Experience

  • Required: Deep, hands-on Avaya Aura delivery across Communication Manager, System/Session Manager, messaging, SBCE, AES, media servers and gateways, and Device Services; Avaya Workplace (formerly Equinox) soft clients; and virtualization (VMware ESXi, AVP) with OVA deployment and legacy to cloud/System Platform migration.
  • Preferred: Avaya Experience Platform (AXP) and CCaaS; AI enablement (virtual agents, agent assist, AI-powered self-service); and voice protocol and telephony security depth (SIP/SIP trunking, H.323, MGCP; certificates, reverse proxy, firewalls).

Qualifications

Experience

  • 8+ years implementing and supporting complex Avaya Aura engagements (planning, configuration, integration, and cutover) in a medium to large organization, including gathering and documenting requirements with business stakeholders.
  • Hands-on preventive maintenance, installation, and administration of Avaya gateways (G450/G430/G350, G650 PN, EGW) and Communication Manager Server 7.x, 8.x, and 10.x.
  • Experience with complex dial plans, call handlers, auto-attendants, and attendant console; bulk configuration tools; contact center functionality (agents, skills, vectors) desirable.
  • Experience with messaging (Aura Messaging, Avaya IX Messaging/OfficeLinx), Breeze and Breeze plug-ins, AADS/Utility Server, and 46xx settings files; several preferred.

Technical Proficiency

  • Server and OS depth: Linux/ESXi administration and System Platform migrations; Linux commands for log analysis; DHCP, DNS, and split-horizon DNS.
  • Integration depth: Application Enablement Services (TSAPI, CVLAN, DMCC) and related integration; remote access and diagnostic tools (VPN, Nectar, web-based).
  • Delivery tooling: Microsoft Dynamics 365/Project Operations for booking, time entry, and delivery operations; AI-powered delivery tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, Claude).

Soft Skills

  • Senior technical presence: leads deployments hands-on and mentors less experienced engineers.
  • Excellent attention to detail; adapts to shifting priorities, competing demands, and timelines.
  • Strong analytical and problem solving skills; manages multiple complex efforts simultaneously.
  • Excellent oral and written communication and customer service skills across all levels of the organization.
  • Collaborative across internal and external teams; comfortable with ambiguity and change.

Education

  • Bachelor’s Degree required; Master’s a plus. Emphasis in a technology field preferred. Equivalent work experience will be considered.

Additional Requirements

  • Avaya certifications strongly valued: ACIS/ACSS or current Avaya certification equivalents; Avaya Aura credentials desirable.
  • VMware certifications preferred; other technical certifications a plus (Cisco networking/telephony, security, or cloud).
  • Availability to work flexible hours as needed, including after hours cutovers.

Physical Requirements

  1. Sitting: Ability to sit for extended periods (up to 80% of the time).
  2. Lifting: Ability to lift or carry objects up to 10 lbs.
  3. Equipment: Frequent use of computer, telephone, and standard office equipment.
  4. Travel: Ability to travel up to 10% for customer installations, cutovers, and training.

QuickBooks Graduates Positioning & Storytelling

Own the positioning and messaging that fuels the QuickBooks Graduates program, working alongside marketing teams, sales, and partner teams who drive its broader execution. Industry & Micro-Vertical Messaging

Go beyond a one-size-fits-all QuickBooks-replacement narrative. Go-to-Market Leadership

Work collaboratively with the broader marketing organization to support end-to-end go-to-market strategies for QuickBooks Graduates campaigns.

Customer-Centered Narratives

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Work hand-in-hand with product, sales, and industry/vertical teams to stay aligned on roadmaps, priorities, and upcoming capabilities relevant to QuickBooks migration. Data-Informed Strategy

Content Experiences & Demos

Support release planning and help keep internal and external teams aligned on positioning as offerings grow and change.

Contribute to partner and customer events through presentations, webinars, and thought leadership sessions — including opportunities to present live — sharing Acumatica's vision and expertise with confidence and authenticity.

Messaging and Positioning

Translate functionality and benefits into real value that resonate with small business buyers, tailoring that value story to both the overarching QuickBooks Graduates program and its industry-specific extensions.

Job Title: Senior Environmental Engineer (Engineer V)

Location: Remote

Description/Job Summary

POSITION DESCRIPTION

This Environmental Engineer V position will be responsible for leading technical execution in design/implementation of feasibility studies, treatability studies, civil and remediation system design, and support during construction for HGL’s portfolio of environmental remediation projects for the USEPA, USACE, NASA, and various agencies across the United States and territories. Projects may include remediation, demolition, mine-waste cleanup, in-situ thermal treatment, landfill cap construction, radioactive soil, contaminated sediment removals, O&M, groundwater treatment systems (both in-situ and pump-n-treat) and stabilization projects.

The Engineer V position is also responsible for supporting the EPA Director and CLIN 2 Program Manager in the leading and managing of the company’s Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) contracts within EPA Region 6 and other regions and ensuring all projects are executed in alignment with client expectations, contractual requirements, and company objectives. This role oversees EPA-related projects and project teams, provides strategic leadership, supports business development efforts within the EPA Region 6 portfolio, and serves as a primary point of contact for Region 6 client engagement. The position also plays a key role in mentoring and developing staff, including project managers, to ensure consistent and successful project delivery.

The Engineer V position has the potential to work fully remotely with occasional travel to project sites and HGL offices. If a candidate resides within commuting distance of an HGL office and would like to work hybrid, that option is also available to them. Preference is for candidates who reside within EPA Region 6 (Arkansas, Louisiana, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Texas).

Responsibilities/Duties

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

The person hired for this role will be responsible for:

  • Direct, manage and lead project engineering design teams.
  • Collaborate with Project Manager and engineers, geologists, CAD/GIS specialists and other technical staff in the development of studies/strategies for remediation for contaminated media.
  • Develop engineering studies, plans, designs, and specifications for the remediation of contaminated media.
  • Develop costs estimates and construction workplans for remedial construction.
  • Supporting Civil and Environmental Design Projects.
  • Ensuring project objectives are met.
  • Project schedule development and review.
  • Quality Control.
  • Mentoring of junior engineering staff.

Staff Management:

  • Support HGL’s EPA program and direct all EPA-related contracts and CLIN (Contract Line-Item Number) project managers within region 6.
  • Support a team of staff, including formal employee mentorship to provide guidance and professional development.
  • Communicate and connect with various departments (proposal development, contracts, chemistry, data management, etc.) to ensure that they are properly coordinating and functioning to support the region.

Project Oversight and Delivery:

  • Ensure EPA Region 6 projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in compliance with project scope of work and contract requirements and client expectations.
  • Conduct routine meetings with project managers to monitor project progress, review deliverables, and provide strategic direction.
  • Guide and enforce company best practices for consistent EPA project execution across teams.
  • Address and resolve project issues and challenges.
  • Serve as a Senior Project Manager on some Region 6 Task Orders.
  • Uphold contract and company required QA/QC and Health and Safety standards.

Client and Stakeholder Engagement:

  • Serve as liaison with EPA Region 6 clients, fostering strong relationships to ensure satisfaction and repeat business.
  • Coordinate with external stakeholders for scope and cost sensitive items including EPA clients and state and local agencies as needed for specific projects.
  • Respond to client inquiries and proactively address client needs to maintain high levels of satisfaction.

Proposal and Business Development:

  • Support, organize and lead proposal efforts for EPA-related opportunities, working closely with technical teams, HGL leadership, and teaming partners to submit high-quality and competitive proposals.
  • Assist in growing the company’s Region 6 EPA portfolio, identifying new opportunities, and contributing to long-term client engagement strategies.
  • Evaluate potential project opportunities for profitability and alignment with company goals.
  • Support planning for and attendance of client sponsored Industry Day events and conferences.

Process Improvement and Standardization:

The role combines Manhattan WMS functional testing, test automation, application support, warehouse operations knowledge, and technical troubleshooting.

jobs.description:
About us

HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.

To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.

Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

Our people

With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our impact

Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.

Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts

Who You Are:

You are the Payroll Lead who owns end-to-end payroll operations for India and the UAE, bringing order, precision, and scale to how we pay our people. You will report to the Senior Manager, Global Payroll, who will provide direction and support as you work in close partnership with HR, Finance, and our external payroll service providers to run the function day to day. You are stepping into a role that’s ready to be transformed – stabilizing payroll operations and service-provider relationships so that every employee is paid accurately and on time, while driving real, measurable gains in operational efficiency. You see yourself as the primary champion for payroll and workforce compliance, holding every payroll cycle to the statutory standards of both geographies.

This is an individual contributor role currently, with no direct reports. Your impact comes from the depth of your expertise and the ownership you take of the function itself.

What You’ll Be Doing:

Payroll

  • Independently lead and govern end-to-end payroll for India and UAE employees, ensuring accuracy and timeliness across all monthly disbursements, including oversight of payroll inputs, processing, and final bank funding.
  • Validate attendance, leave, variable pay, incentives, reimbursements, and full-and-final settlement inputs against HRIS and finance records before each payroll run.
  • Perform rigorous reviews of payroll registers, variance reports, CTC, and reconciliation files to validate data integrity and ensure alignment with financial controls and internal audit standards.
  • Stabilize and optimize relationships with external payroll service providers by setting clear performance benchmarks and conducting regular audits to drive service excellence.
  • Transform the current payroll ecosystem by identifying process bottlenecks and implementing technology-driven solutions that increase automation and reduce manual intervention.

Compliance

  • Champion workforce compliance across teams by serving as the primary subject matter expert on Indian labour laws, Provident Fund, ESIC, Income Tax regulations, and Payroll SOX requirements.
  • Mitigate corporate risk by leading statutory filing activities and ensuring monthly, quarterly, and annual payroll-related returns are submitted accurately to government authorities.
  • Support internal, statutory, and external audits; prepare payroll-related MIS, accruals, and reconciliations for Finance; and maintain audit-ready documentation at all times.
  • Track changes in Indian and UAE labour law, tax regulations, and social security requirements, and proactively update processes and stakeholders.

Employee Support

  • Act as the first point of contact for payroll, tax, and benefits queries; ensure payslips, Form 16 / tax documents, and salary certificates are issued accurately and on time.
  • Work closely with HR, Finance, Legal, and Total Rewards teams on compensation changes, benefits and equity administration, and new market/entity payroll setup.

System Management

  • Own and administer Darwinbox as the system of record for payroll, ensuring data integrity and seamless flow between the HR and payroll modules.
  • Manage payroll-related configuration, user access, and integrations between Darwinbox and downstream finance/banking systems.
  • Troubleshoot system issues and liaise with the Darwinbox support/People Tech team on fixes, upgrades, and enhancements.
  • Drive automation of payroll workflows within Darwinbox to reduce manual intervention and improve turnaround time.

What You’ll Bring:

  • 8+ years of hands-on payroll experience, with proven ownership of end-to-end India payroll processing and statutory compliance.
  • Working knowledge of UAE/India payroll practices.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Finance, HR, or a related field; a payroll or labour law certification (e.g., CPP or an India payroll compliance certification) is a plus.
  • Hands-on experience with payroll/HRIS platforms such as GreytHR, Keka, ADP, or SAP SuccessFactors.
  • Prior expertise with Darwinbox is an added advantage.
  • Strong Excel/data-reconciliation skills and comfort working with large employee datasets.
  • High attention to detail, strong ownership, and the ability to handle sensitive compensation data with discretion.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to manage multiple stakeholders and deadlines across time zones (India and UAE).
  • Prior experience in a fast-paced, multi-entity, or global SaaS/tech environment is a plus.

Product Owner, Wealth Experience

We’re seeking a Product Owner to support the design and delivery of the wealth experience within NYL360. jobs.excerpt: About Knotch We're a growth-stage technology company helping brands optimize content performance and apply AI to modern marketing.
jobs.description:
About Knotch

We're a growth-stage technology company helping brands optimize content performance and apply AI to modern marketing. Our culture is fast-paced, entrepreneurial, and highly adaptable—we move quickly, test ideas, and evolve with our customers.

Through the Knotch platform, brands can measure the impact of their content, identify what drives results, and continuously improve performance across channels. By combining performance data, strategic insights, and AI-driven capabilities, we help marketing teams make smarter decisions and get more impact from every piece of content they produce.

About the position

You'll split your time between two front ends at very different stages.

Knotch ACE, generates web experiences from AI in real time. Rather than serving fixed pages, our backend streams typed component descriptions and the front end assembles them into a React tree as they arrive. It's Next.js App Router and TypeScript in a monorepo, live for several enterprise brands, each with its own theming and deployment.

Knotch One is a mature React application that customers use daily, built on Redux, GraphQL and styled-components, with data visualization at its core.

Between them there's a good mix of greenfield design work and the kind of careful change you make in a codebase with real users. We're looking for someone who's happy doing both.

Responsibilities

  • Build features across both applications, working to each one's existing conventions.
  • Develop the component system that renders streamed, AI-generated layouts — schemas, renderers, and the contracts between them.
  • Work on multi-tenant theming: design tokens, per-brand configuration, client-specific variants.
  • Build and maintain embeds that run our product inside customer websites.
  • Set standards for testing, accessibility, and performance.
  • Work with backend engineers on API and streaming contracts, including where the line between front end and backend actually sits.
  • Write the approach down before you build it, and raise blockers, risks and disagreements early rather than after they've cost time.
  • Ramp yourself up on unfamiliar parts of the product and codebase, and mentor others through code review, pairing, and written design.

How we Work

Knotch moves quickly and the team is small, so you'll wear a few hats — you'll own features end to end, work directly with backend, data and product, and see what you build in front of enterprise clients in weeks rather than quarters.

That pace runs on writing. Design and decisions happen in docs and threads here: you'll write the approach before you build it, keep people posted on where things stand, flag risks as soon as you see them, and say what you think when you disagree — including with us. Silence reads as agreement, so if something looks wrong, say so.

It also runs on people who find their own way in. We'll point you at the right person and the right part of the codebase, and questions are always welcome — but the engineers who do well here read the code, form a view, and bring it back for a second opinion rather than a walkthrough. Everyone teaches, and everyone is expected to come up to speed fast.

From there, the work is yours to run with.

Skills & Experience

  • 6+ years building React applications in production.
  • TypeScript day to day, including typing data that arrives at runtime.
  • Next.js App Router, or another framework with a server/client rendering split — Remix, Nuxt, SvelteKit.
  • Experience in a large codebase with history, where the work meant fitting into earlier decisions rather than starting clean.
  • CSS at scale — utility-first (Tailwind) or CSS-in-JS (styled-components, Emotion), and styling systems built on tokens or theme objects.
  • Accessible UI work — keyboard navigation, ARIA, and testing against WCAG.
  • Data visualization — ECharts, D3, Recharts or similar.
  • Writing tests alongside features — Vitest, Jest, Testing Library or similar.
  • Clear written communication, and a track record of working without close supervision: scoping your own work, unblocking yourself, and telling people what you need.

Nice to Have

  • Runtime schema validation — Zod, Valibot or similar.
  • Streaming or incremental UI — SSE, WebSockets.
  • Monorepo tooling — pnpm workspaces, Turborepo, Nx.
  • Design tokens and multi-tenant theming.
  • Embedding JavaScript into third-party sites — iframes, CSP, sandboxing.
  • Client state management at scale (Redux, Zustand or similar) against a typed API layer, GraphQL or REST.
  • Using AI-assisted tooling to move faster, and a view on where it helps and where it doesn't.

Our Benefits and Perks

  • Salary -The expected salary range for this role is $135,000 - $175,000 CAD depending on experience.
  • Health Benefits - Through our employer of record (EOR) relationship with Globalization Partners, we're proud to offer comprehensive health benefits.
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Paid Holidays
  • Wellness Perks
  • Daily Company Break

About Riot Platforms

Riot’s (NASDAQ: RIOT) vision is to be the world’s most trusted platform for powering and building digital infrastructure. Riot’s mission is to empower the future of digital infrastructure by positively impacting the sectors, networks, and communities that we touch. We believe that the combination of an innovative spirit and strong community partnership allows us to achieve best-in-class execution and create successful outcomes.

Who we are

At Riot, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure. Our team members have unparalleled opportunities to work on groundbreaking initiatives. Through technical excellence and strategic execution, Riot has positioned itself as a leader in the industry driving advancements that continue to set new benchmarks in digital infrastructure.

We are trailblazers. Problem solvers. People who thrive in fast paced environments, communicate clearly, and bring relentless focus to efficiency and execution.

About the role

The Director, Risk Management owns Riot's most time-critical GRC pillar. This role steps directly into that execution environment — timelines do not pause for onboarding.

This pillar is intentionally scoped: Risk Management owns the external auditor relationship, the evidence pipeline, the enterprise risk register, the POA&M lifecycle, and the ISO 27001 audit readiness and certification audit track. You own risk identification, risk quantification, audit execution, and the remediation lifecycle that closes gaps across all pillars.

You will report to the Senior Director, GRC and serve as Riot's primary relationship owner with external auditors across SOC 1, SOC 2, and ISO 27001. You will partner directly with the CFO on SOX obligations and with Internal Audit on shared ITGC methodology. In critical operations, you will engage mining site and data center leadership to ensure operational risks are captured, assessed, and reflected in the enterprise risk register.

What you'll do

  • Own end-to-end execution of SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II audits: scoping, control walkthroughs, evidence collection, auditor liaison, management response drafting, and remediation tracking — you are the primary point of contact for all external audit activity.
  • Lead the ISO 27001:2022 audit readiness and certification audit track — coordinating evidence, managing the certification audit relationship, and driving the program to on-schedule certification under the governance of the Sr. Director, GRC.
  • Serve as the primary liaison to Internal Audit for SOX ITGC coordination — establishing a shared control inventory, aligning testing methodologies, dividing walkthroughs to eliminate duplication, and maintaining a joint remediation cadence.
  • Build and operate the Riot enterprise risk register: define the risk taxonomy, conduct risk assessments across all business units including mining and data center operations, tier risks by likelihood and impact, and maintain a living register updated no less than quarterly.
  • Develop and maintain the KRI/KPI framework for executive and Board-level risk reporting — translating risk register outputs into leading indicators that give leadership actionable visibility into Riot's risk posture.
  • Run the POA&M (Plan of Action & Milestones) program: intake all audit findings and control gaps across all GRC pillars, assign ownership, track remediation progress, escalate stalled items, and report status to the Sr. Director on a defined cadence.
  • Build continuous audit-readiness infrastructure: design repeatable evidence pipelines, drive evidence collection automation where possible, and eliminate point-in-time audit scrambles by maintaining a year-round audit-ready posture.

What you'll bring

  • 8–12+ years of progressive GRC, IT audit, or enterprise risk management experience, with direct, hands-on ownership of SOC 1 and/or SOC 2 Type II audits — required, not supporting-role exposure.
  • ISO 27001 Lead Implementer certification — required. Must have credentialed implementation experience to own the audit execution and certification track.
  • Working knowledge of SOX ITGC requirements at a publicly traded company, with demonstrated experience coordinating GRC work with an Internal Audit function.
  • Proven experience building or operating an enterprise risk register, risk taxonomy, and KRI/KPI reporting framework for executive audiences.
  • Experience owning the external auditor relationship — managing audit timelines, evidence requests, walkthrough coordination, and management response drafting across multiple concurrent audit programs.
  • Strong POA&M and remediation lifecycle management: tracking, escalating, and closing audit findings across cross-functional control owners.
  • Familiarity with at least one additional security framework beyond SOC 2 — ISO 27001, NIST CSF, or NIST 800-53.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication — ability to present risk posture and audit status in executive-ready formats for Board Audit Committee reporting.
  • Preferred: CISA or CRISC certification; experience in critical infrastructure, data center, energy, or digital asset environments; exposure to OT/ICS risk environments.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive Salary: Base range (commensurate with experience) + bonus + sign-on equity grant.
  • Long-Term Growth: Eligible to participate in Riot’s equity incentive programs and share in the success you help build.
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan: Incudes a generous company match.
  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans.
  • Wellness & Lifestyle Perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, and more to support your life both in and out of work.

Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Backblaze is the object storage leader in the open cloud movement, fueling customer success with cloud storage built purposefully to unlock budgets, unburden administrators, and unleash innovators. Together with our partners, we’re helping customers break free from the restrictive, overpriced legacy solutions that hold them back, and blaze forward with the full power of the open cloud in their hands.

Founded in 2007, we scaled the business with less than $3 million in outside funding until 2021, when we did a traditional IPO on the Nasdaq stock exchange. Today, Backblaze generates over $100m in revenue and is the leading specialized storage cloud, managing over three billion gigabytes of data storage for 500K+ customers in 175+ countries, including businesses, developers, IT professionals, and individuals.

But while there is a lot to celebrate in our past, there is almost as much opportunity ahead of us. We’re seeking a B2 Principal Product Manager to join our team!

About the Role

We are seeking an ambitious and accomplished Principal Product Manager to join our Product team. Backblaze’s B2 cloud object storage offers multi-exabyte, S3-compatible, globally available object storage that unlocks app builder innovation across AI neoclouds and traditional hyperscalers at a fraction of the cost of traditional cloud infrastructure hyperscalers.

The Principal Product Manager for B2 will work closely with key stakeholders to understand the evolution of cloud storage and the customer problems in the space, and determine product strategies and roadmap to address those problems. jobs.excerpt: On this journey for over 12 years, Qventus is leading the transformation of healthcare.
jobs.description:
On this journey for over 12 years, Qventus is leading the transformation of healthcare. We enable hospitals to focus on what matters most: patient care. Our innovative solutions harness the power of machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science to deliver exceptional outcomes and empower care teams to anticipate and resolve issues before they arise.

Our success in rapid scale across the globe is backed by some of the world's leading investors. At Qventus, you will have the opportunity to work with an exceptional, mission-driven team across the globe, and the ability to directly impact the lives of patients. We’re inspired to work with healthcare leaders on our founding vision and unlock world-class medicine through world-class operations.

About the role:

We're looking for a Senior / Staff Analytics Program Lead to own the analytics product program across our global Analytics organization. While our solution analytics leads own the definitions and insights for a single solution, this role owns the analytics product function as a system: how analytics products get built, how they hold together across solutions, and how fast we can ship the next one. You are accountable for the coherence, quality, and velocity of everything the analytics function delivers, internal and external, and for steering the function toward more self-serve and agentic analytics, where trusted metric definitions let customers, internal teams, and AI agents answer more questions without an analyst in the loop.

This is a hybrid role. Most of your time goes to running the program: enforcing and evolving the analytics standards and ways of working that let each pod ship correctly, scoping and sequencing work across solutions, and partnering with platform, data/BI engineering, and context architecture to shape the technical & semantic foundations our analytics products are built on, especially as we scale towards enabling increased self-service with AI tools. The rest is hands-on. You will jump into a domain as an individual contributor when the hardest problems need you, both to unblock the team and to stay closely aligned the work you're setting the bar for. If you are energized by taking a pattern you know works and re-establishing it at a broader scale, this is that role.

Key Responsibilities:

At Qventus, Analytics is treated as a first-class product, rather than a secondary output. As the Analytics Program Lead, you will:

  • Own delivery of coherent, high-quality, on-time analytics products across solutions, and hold the bar for products that are stable, maintainable, and easy to iterate and enhance over time
  • Increase the velocity at which we build and ship analytics products by enforcing and shaping standards, developing analytics AI skills and context, and evolving team structures, in partnership with our Data Engineering, BI Engineering, and Product teams
  • Lead the solution analytics leads as their manager, owning how the analytics team works day to day, scoping and sequencing work across solutions, and keeping people unblocked and focused
  • Partner with our Data Platform Manager and Data Context & Semantic Architect to shape the BI platform and semantic architecture that supports both our standard embedded analytics products and the move toward self-service analytics (incl. Analytics agents)
  • Stay hands-on, contributing directly as an IC in a domain when the work demands it, to unblock the team and to keep close to the craft you're holding others to

What We're Looking For:

  • Demonstrated program ownership of a technical function: you have scoped, sequenced, and shipped analytics or data work across multiple parallel workstreams and held ultimate responsibility for quality and coherence, not just your own output
  • Strong analytical rigor: you can take an ambiguous question to a precise, defensible answer, with the hands-on depth (SQL/dbt, modern warehouse and BI) to do the work yourself and set the standard, not just review against it
  • A systems-builder instinct: you turn what works into repeatable process, standards, and enforcement that keep running without you, rather than holding the function together through personal effort
  • Cross-functional influence across teams you don't directly control, with a track record of driving alignment when interpretations differ and holding durable working relationships with platform, engineering, and architecture partners
  • Comfort with ambiguity and scale: you can take a coherent way of working that you've proven and re-establish it at broader scale across solutions and teams

It's a Plus if You Have…

  • Expertise in the healthcare domain and familiarity with healthcare operational data, clinical workflows, hospital operations, or common healthcare measurement challenges
  • Experience scaling an analytics function at a growing company, taking something that worked at smaller scale and rebuilding it as a system others can run
  • Familiarity with data governance, metric governance, or semantic layer concepts, especially where consistency across teams, solutions, or customer implementations is critical
  • Experience with data logic implemented in dbt and data visualization in Sigma, and with knowledge management systems for documenting metric definitions and analytical decisions
  • Exposure to AI-enabled analytics, natural language analytics, or agentic analytics workflows, especially where high-quality metric definitions and trusted analytical context are required for safe and useful AI outputs

Compensation for this role is based on market data and takes into account a variety of factors, including location, skills, qualifications, and prior relevant experience. Salary is just one part of the total rewards package at Qventus. We also offer a range of benefits and perks, including Open Paid Time Off, paid parental leave, professional development, wellness and technology stipends, a generous employee referral bonus, and employee stock option awards.

  • Manage and respond to data privacy incidents and data subject requests.
  • Educate employees on data privacy best practices and raise awareness throughout the organization.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for regulatory authorities and individuals regarding privacy-related matters.

Requirements

  • Strong knowledge of global privacy laws and regulations, including GDPR and CCPA.

jobs.description:
1. Identificación del Cargo

Título del cargo: Carrier Relations and Routing

Ubicación: Colombia (Hibrido)

Alcance geográfico: Colombia, Venezuela, México y Centroamérica
Tipo de relación: Gestión de relaciones y optimización de enrutamiento (routing) con operadoras (carriers) de telecomunicaciones
2. Propósito del Cargo
El Carrier Agent es responsable de establecer, desarrollar y mantener relaciones comerciales sólidas y duraderas con operadoras de telecomunicaciones en Colombia, Venezuela, México y Centroamérica, así como de monitorear y contribuir a la optimización del enrutamiento (routing) del tráfico con dichas operadoras. Este cargo es clave para asegurar acuerdos beneficiosos, coordinar operaciones conjuntas, dar seguimiento a la calidad y el costo de las rutas, y representar a la empresa como un socio confiable y cercano ante las operadoras, todo esto gestionado de forma remota pero con un nivel de cercanía y calidez propio de una relación presencial.
3. Responsabilidades Principales
• Construir y mantener relaciones comerciales cercanas y de confianza con operadoras de telecomunicaciones en Colombia, Venezuela, México y Centroamérica
• Actuar como punto de contacto principal entre la empresa y las operadoras, gestionando la comunicación de manera fluida, cordial y profesional.
• Negociar términos comerciales, tarifas y acuerdos de interconexión que beneficien a ambas partes.
• Monitorear el desempeño de las relaciones con cada operadora, identificando oportunidades de mejora o expansión del negocio.
• Monitorear indicadores técnicos de las rutas de tráfico (SMS y/o voz) por operadora, como tasa de entrega, latencia y calidad, en coordinación con los equipos técnicos y de producto.
• Contribuir a la optimización de rutas (Least Cost Routing) evaluando costo, calidad y capacidad de cada operadora.
• Detectar y escalar oportunamente problemas de enrutamiento (caídas de entrega, filtrado, rutas grises) ante las operadoras y las áreas internas correspondientes.
• Coordinar reuniones virtuales periódicas con las operadoras para fortalecer el vínculo y dar seguimiento a compromisos pendientes.
• Resolver de manera proactiva y diplomática cualquier inconveniente o fricción que surja en la relación comercial.
• Identificar nuevas oportunidades de negocio y potenciales operadoras con las cuales establecer alianzas.
• Reportar periódicamente a la gerencia sobre el estado de las relaciones, negociaciones en curso y resultados obtenidos.
• Representar a la empresa en eventos, llamadas y espacios de networking del sector, incluso de forma virtual.
4. Perfil del Candidato
Habilidades interpersonales (esenciales para este cargo)
• Carisma natural y facilidad para generar empatía y confianza desde el primer contacto.
• Sociabilidad genuina: disfruta conectar con personas de distintas culturas, países y estilos de trabajo.
• Excelentes habilidades de comunicación oral y escrita, tanto en español como, idealmente, en inglés.
• Capacidad comprobada para construir relaciones comerciales fuertes y de largo plazo, incluso a distancia.
• Habilidad para leer el contexto cultural y adaptar su estilo de comunicación según el interlocutor (Colombia, Venezuela, México, Centroamérica).
• Actitud positiva, proactiva y orientada al servicio, incluso bajo presión o en negociaciones complejas.
Formación y experiencia
• Formación en Telecomunicaciones, Negocios Internacionales, Administración, Relaciones Comerciales o áreas afines.
• Experiencia previa en roles de account management, ventas B2B, relaciones con carriers o gestión comercial, preferiblemente en el sector telco.
• Conocimiento del mercado de telecomunicaciones en Colombia, Venezuela, México y Centroamérica (deseable).
• Experiencia trabajando de forma remota y gestionando relaciones interculturales.
Competencias técnicas
• Manejo de herramientas de videoconferencia, CRM, Google Workspace, Slack y Hubspot (deseable).
• Conocimiento de conceptos de enrutamiento de tráfico de telecomunicaciones (Least Cost Routing, calidad de ruta, tasa de entrega) (deseable, se puede entrenar).
• Manejo de herramientas o plataformas de monitoreo de tráfico y reporting de KPIs (deseable).
• Capacidad de análisis de tráfico, tarifas, acuerdos de interconexión e indicadores de calidad de ruta (deseable, se puede entrenar).
• Organización y disciplina para el trabajo remoto autónomo.
5. Condiciones del Cargo
• Modalidad: 100% remoto, con base en Colombia.
• Disponibilidad para reuniones en distintos horarios según la contraparte (Colombia, Venezuela, México y Centroamérica).
• Disponibilidad para viajar ocasionalmente si la empresa lo requiere (según necesidad del negocio).
6. Perfil Ideal en Una Frase
Buscamos una persona carismática, sociable y con habilidades naturales para conectar y generar confianza, capaz de convertir cada interacción con una operadora en el inicio de una relación comercial sólida y duradera, sin importar la distancia.

 

JOB DESCRIPTION

Carrier Relations and Routing — Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico and Central America (Remote)

1. Position Identification

Job title: Carrier Relations and Routing

Location: Colombia (Hybrid position)

Geographic scope: Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico and Central America
Type of relationship: Management of relationships and routing optimization with telecommunications operators (carriers)
Work arrangement: Remote work with constant, direct interaction with counterparts across the region

2. Purpose of the Position

The Carrier Agent is responsible for establishing, developing and maintaining strong, long-lasting commercial relationships with telecommunications operators in Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico and Central America, as well as monitoring and contributing to the optimization of traffic routing with those operators. This position is key to securing mutually beneficial agreements, coordinating joint operations, tracking route quality and cost, and representing the company as a trusted, close partner before the operators — all managed remotely, but with the same closeness and warmth as an in-person relationship.

3. Key Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain close, trust-based commercial relationships with telecommunications operators in Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico and Central America.
    • Act as the main point of contact between the company and the operators, managing communication in a smooth, cordial and professional manner.
    • Negotiate commercial terms, rates and interconnection agreements that benefit both parties.
    • Monitor the performance of the relationship with each operator, identifying opportunities to improve or expand the business.
    • Monitor technical route performance indicators (SMS and/or voice) per operator, such as delivery rate, latency and quality, in coordination with technical and product teams.
    • Contribute to route optimization (Least Cost Routing) by evaluating cost, quality and capacity of each operator.
    • Proactively detect and escalate routing issues (delivery drops, filtering, grey routes) to operators and the relevant internal teams.
    • Coordinate regular virtual meetings with the operators to strengthen the relationship and follow up on outstanding commitments.
    • Proactively and diplomatically resolve any issue or friction that arises in the commercial relationship.
    • Identify new business opportunities and potential operators with which to establish partnerships.
    • Report regularly to management on the status of relationships, ongoing negotiations and results achieved.
    • Represent the company at industry events, calls and networking spaces, including virtually.

4. Candidate Profile

Interpersonal skills (essential for this position)
• Natural charisma and an ease for building empathy and trust from the very first contact.
• Genuine sociability: enjoys connecting with people from different cultures, countries and working styles.
• Excellent oral and written communication skills, in Spanish and, ideally, in English.
• Proven ability to build strong, long-term commercial relationships, even remotely.
• Ability to read the cultural context and adapt communication style to each counterpart (Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico, Central America).
• Positive, proactive and service-oriented attitude, even under pressure or in complex negotiations.

Education and experience

  • Education in Telecommunications, International Business, Business Administration, Commercial Relations or related fields.
    • Previous experience in account management, B2B sales, carrier relations or commercial management roles, preferably in the telco sector.
    • Knowledge of the telecommunications market in Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico and Central America (desirable).
    • Experience working remotely and managing cross-cultural relationships.
    Technical skills
    • Proficiency with videoconferencing tools, CRM, Google Workspace, Slack and HubSpot (desirable).
    • Familiarity with telecom traffic routing concepts (Least Cost Routing, route quality, delivery rate) (desirable; can be trained).
    • Proficiency with traffic monitoring tools or KPI reporting platforms (desirable).
    • Ability to analyze traffic, rates, interconnection agreements and route quality indicators (desirable; can be trained).
    • Organization and discipline for autonomous remote work.

5. Position Conditions

  • Work arrangement: hybrid, based in Colombia.
    • Availability for meetings at different times depending on the counterpart (Colombia, Venezuela, Mexico, Central America).
    • Availability to travel occasionally if required by the company (based on business needs).

6. Ideal Profile in One Sentence

We are looking for a charismatic, sociable person with a natural ability to connect and build trust — someone able to turn every interaction with an operator into the beginning of a strong, lasting commercial relationship, no matter the distance.

Location

This position will be located in Colombia. You will get to experience a company that believes in small teams for maximum impact; seeks well-rounded talent to ensure a full perspective on our customers’ experience, understands that this is a marathon, not a sprint; that continuously and purposefully builds an inclusive culture where everyone is able to do and be the best version of themselves.

About Us

Since 2001, Messangi has been connecting companies to their customers on billions of devices around the world. Our versatile and reliable platforms have been built in-house by some of the top engineers in the business. To power our operations, we have world-class teams in 7 countries willing to go the extra mile to meet our customers’ needs. Today, top mobile operators, global banks, and retailers rely on Messangi to solve their customer communication and engagement

jobs.title: Manager/Lead, Salesforce Administration
jobs.excerpt: We are looking for an experienced Senior Salesforce Administrator to lead the day-to-day stewardship and continued evolution of our Salesforce ecosystem.
jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced Senior Salesforce Administrator to lead the day-to-day stewardship and continued evolution of our Salesforce ecosystem. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will guide and develop a team, own critical platform controls, and remain directly involved in the design, configuration, release and support of business-critical solutions.

The role is accountable for the reliability, security, scalability and maintainability of our Salesforce estate, with particular focus on Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, and the APIs and integrations that connect Salesforce to Slack and other enterprise platforms. You will balance rapid delivery with strong governance, helping the organisation get more value from Salesforce without increasing operational or security risk.

What you will be accountable for

1. Team leadership and operating model

  • Lead and develop the Salesforce team, setting clear priorities, standards and expectations while creating an environment of ownership, learning and constructive challenge.

  • Act as the senior escalation point, providing calm, evidence-led direction during incidents, complex delivery decisions and stakeholder conflicts.

  • Shape the team operating model, including capacity planning, work allocation, skills development, recruitment support and the effective use of specialist partners.

  • Build sustainable capability, through coaching, documentation, peer review and reducing dependency on individual team members or external suppliers.

2. Salesforce platform ownership

  • Own the health and evolution of Sales Cloud, Service Cloud and Experience Cloud, ensuring the platform supports commercial, customer-service and operational processes effectively.

  • Set and enforce platform standards, covering configuration, automation, data models, naming conventions, documentation, testing and technical debt.

  • Remain hands-on where needed, including complex Flow automation, permissions, validation rules, objects, page layouts, Lightning pages, reports, dashboards, analytics and troubleshooting.

  • Own day-to-day system administration, including user administration, joiner/mover/leaver processing, delegated administration and routine platform hygiene.

  • Configure and maintain Experience Cloud portals, including external sharing rules, guest user access, community settings, and partner- or customer-facing experiences.

  • Maintain a clear platform roadmap that balances strategic improvements, regulatory or security obligations, operational resilience, and business demand.

  • Control platform lifecycle changes, including Salesforce seasonal releases, feature adoption, deprecations, sandbox strategy and environment management.

  • Evaluate and deploy AppExchange packages, assessing them against business requirements, security review status, licence cost, support model and long-term maintainability.

3. Integrations, APIs and operational monitoring

  • Own the operational oversight of Salesforce integrations, including interfaces with Slack and other core enterprise applications.

  • Administer and maintain key business integrations.

  • Establish effective Slack API monitoring to cover authentication failures, token or certificate expirations, API errors, rate limits, latency, message delivery failures, and unexpected usage patterns.

  • Define monitoring and alerting standards, with meaningful thresholds, named owners, support runbooks, escalation paths and service-level expectations.

  • Protect integration reliability by overseeing connected apps, OAuth scopes, named credentials, integration users, event-driven services and API consumption.

  • Lead incident response and problem management, ensuring root causes are understood, corrective actions are completed and recurring failures are designed out.

4. Security, access and control posture

  • Own the Salesforce security posture, working with Security, IT and Risk teams to maintain proportionate, auditable controls.

  • Design and maintain the org-wide sharing and security architecture, including organisation-wide defaults (OWD), role hierarchy, sharing rules, permission sets and permission-set groups, and field-level security.

  • Apply least-privilege access, with appropriate segregation of duties and regular remediation of accumulated or excessive entitlements.

  • Govern identities and privileged access, including SSO and MFA (working knowledge of Okta or a comparable identity provider), service accounts, integration users, delegated administration and joiner/mover/leaver controls.

  • Lead regular security audits and access reviews to evidence least-privilege compliance and drive timely remediation of findings.

  • Partner with IT and Security on platform audits and compliance, including SOC 2 and GDPR obligations, control evidence and audit response.

  • Review platform risk signals, such as login anomalies, API usage, configuration changes, installed packages and connected-app behaviour, using the monitoring capabilities available in the Salesforce estate.

  • Protect sensitive information through sound data-access design, retention controls, masking or anonymisation in non-production environments, and responsible vendor access.

5. Licensing, certificates and lifecycle management

  • Optimise licence usage and forecasting across Sales Cloud, Service Cloud and Experience Cloud, including reharvesting, right-sizing and renewal input.

  • Monitor and manage certificate lifecycles, including SSL and SAML signing certificates, to prevent avoidable authentication or integration outages.

  • Manage connected app and OAuth lifecycles, with a maintained inventory, named owners, expiry tracking and proactive renewal ahead of failure.

  • Provide clear cost and entitlement visibility, so licence, package and integration spend is understood, challenged and aligned to realised value.

6. Delivery, release and DevOps

  • Own a transparent and prioritised delivery backlog, working with business stakeholders to clarify outcomes, value, dependencies and acceptance criteria.

  • Maintain disciplined release management, with source control, peer review, automated or repeatable deployment, regression testing, rollback planning and release communications.

  • Execute version-controlled releases through GitHub, using branch strategy, pull requests, peer approval and traceable change history as the standard route to production.

  • Maintain documentation for all configuration and change management, so the estate remains understandable, auditable and supportable by more than one person.

  • Improve platform support, using clear service measures, triage processes, knowledge articles, problem records and trend analysis.

  • Manage technical debt deliberately, making risks and trade-offs visible and ensuring remediation is planned alongside new demand.

  • Partner effectively with vendors, holding delivery partners to clear outcomes, quality standards, documentation and knowledge-transfer commitments.

7. Data quality and platform insight

  • Champion trustworthy Salesforce data, including ownership, validation, duplicate management, integration reconciliation and remediation of recurring data-quality issues.

  • Provide actionable platform insight, using dashboards and regular reporting on adoption, automation failures, API consumption, incidents, release quality, access risk and technical debt.

  • Support sound architecture decisions, challenging unnecessary customisation and promoting maintainable, scalable use of standard Salesforce capabilities and enterprise-level data modelling.

8. AI, Agentforce and emerging capabilities

  • Help evaluate and safely adopt Agentforce, Salesforce AI capabilities and adjacent enterprise AI tools where they can improve employee or customer outcomes.

  • Support responsible AI governance, including data access, grounding, human oversight, prompt and agent testing, monitoring, auditability and change control.

  • Contribute practical experience with Claude or comparable models, especially where AI services interact with Salesforce, Slack, knowledge content, workflows or customer data.

  • Separate experimentation from production readiness, ensuring AI-enabled solutions meet the same security, reliability and support standards as other business-critical capabilities.

Leadership behaviours

  • Service-minded ownership: you treat Salesforce as a critical business service, not simply a collection of projects.

  • Wise pragmatism: you balance speed, usability, maintainability, cost and risk rather than optimising for only one dimension.

  • Constructive challenge: you can say no, or not yet, with clear evidence and a practical route forward.

  • Calm accountability: you take ownership when problems arise without creating blame or hiding uncomfortable facts.

  • Enabling leadership: you give people clarity and support while building their confidence, judgement and independence.

  • Clear communication: you make technical issues understandable and keep stakeholders informed before uncertainty becomes surprise.

Key working relationships

The role will work closely with Sales, Revenue Operations, Customer Service, Finance, Security, Enterprise Architecture, IT Operations, Data and Integration teams, as well as Salesforce and specialist implementation partners.

Essential

  • 7+ years as a Salesforce Administrator in large, multi-team environments, with substantial hands-on responsibility for administration, configuration and operational support in a complex production environment.

  • Salesforce Administrator certification (required).

  • Proven people leadership, including line management, coaching, performance support, work prioritisation and development of Salesforce administrators or platform specialists.

  • Deep practical knowledge of Sales Cloud and Service Cloud, including their security, automation, data and service-management implications.

  • Deep Salesforce security expertise, covering organisation-wide defaults, role hierarchies, sharing models, permission sets, field-level security, identity, privileged access, connected apps and audit controls.

  • Hands-on Experience Cloud capability, including external sharing models, guest access and community configuration.

  • Proven Salesforce DevOps and change-management experience using GitHub, including version-controlled deployment workflows, pull-request review and release governance.

  • Experience operating API-led integrations, including monitoring, troubleshooting, authentication, limits, failure handling and coordination across technical teams.

  • Experience managing SSL and authentication certificates and maintaining integration health.

  • Strong declarative delivery capability, particularly Flow, data modelling, validation, Lightning configuration, reporting and environment management.

  • Sound release and change-management experience, including sandbox strategy, source control, testing, deployment governance and production support.

  • Confident stakeholder management, with the ability to translate between commercial priorities, user needs, technical constraints and risk.

  • Strong solution and design judgement, with a good understanding of platform architecture and enterprise-level data modelling.

Desirable

  • Salesforce Advanced Administrator certification (preferred), or other relevant credentials such as Platform App Builder, Service Cloud Consultant or an appropriate Agentforce/AI accreditation.

  • Experience administering Ironclad, Qualtrics and Slack CRM / Sales Elevate, or directly comparable CLM, survey and Slack-CRM tooling.

  • Agentforce or Salesforce AI experience, including agent design, grounding, guardrails, evaluation or operational monitoring.

  • Experience with Claude or other enterprise AI platforms, particularly in governed, data-sensitive business workflows.

  • Experience with Slack platform capabilities and APIs, including enterprise integrations, apps, workflows, authentication and observability.

  • Working knowledge of Okta or a comparable enterprise identity provider.

  • Exposure to complementary enterprise platforms, such as NetSuite, MuleSoft, Celigo, Boomi, Workato, Zapier, identity providers or data platforms.

  • Experience in a SaaS, technology or high-growth environment, where Salesforce supports complex B2B go-to-market and customer-service processes

Our Values

Collaboration is our superpower

  • We uncover rich perspectives across the world
  • Success happens together
  • We deliver across borders.

Innovation is in our blood

  • We’re pioneers in our industry
  • Our curiosity is insatiable
  • We bring the best ideas to life.

We do what we say

  • We’re accountable for our work and actions
  • Excellence comes as standard
  • We’re open, honest and kind, always.

We are caring

  • We learn from each other’s experiences
  • Stop and listen; every opinion matters
  • We embrace diversity, equity and inclusion.

More About Cint

We’re proud to be recognised in Newsweek’s 2025 Global Top 100 Most Loved Workplaces®, reflecting our commitment to a culture of trust, respect, and employee growth.

In June 2021, Cint acquired Berlin-based GapFish – the world’s largest ISO certified online panel community in the DACH region – and in January 2022, completed the acquisition of US-based Lucid – a programmatic research technology platform that provides access to first-party survey data in over 110 countries.

Cint Group AB (publ), listed on Nasdaq Stockholm, this growth has made Cint a strong global platform with teams across its many global offices, including Stockholm, London, New York, New Orleans, Singapore, Tokyo and Sydney. (www.cint.com)

Additionally, in a world of AI, we want our candidates to understand our approach to the use of AI during the interview and hiring process, so we'd appreciate you reading our AI usage guide.

Who We Are

Cint is a pioneer in research technology (ResTech). Our customers use the Cint platform to post questions and get answers from real people to build business strategies, confidently publish research, accurately measure the impact of digital advertising, and more. The Cint platform is built on a programmatic marketplace, which is the world’s largest, with nearly 300 million respondents in over 150 countries who consent to sharing their opinions, motivations, and behaviours.

We are feeding the world’s curiosity!

  • Test automation

Juno leverages collective bargaining power to secure better student loan rates for students. With 290,000+ members and over $2B in negotiated loan volume, we've proven that group buying works.
